cases.description: A newly created Zone with no records should produce an empty master‑file representation. toString() must return the same empty string as toMasterFile().

group: Zone with a single SOA record

cases.description: Create a Zone, add a single SOARecord (domain example.com, TTL 3600, primary NS ns1.example.com, etc.). The master‑file format for a SOA is a single line ending with a newline. toString() must return exactly that line.

group: Zone with NS and A records

cases.expected:
"example.org. 3600 IN NS ns1.example.org.
example.org. 3600 IN NS ns2.example.org.
www.example.org. 3600 IN A 192.0.2.1
"
cases.description: Populate a Zone with two NS records for the zone apex and one A record for a host. The master‑file representation consists of three lines in the order they were added. toString() must return the concatenated string.

group: Zone with mixed record types (SOA, NS, MX, TXT)

cases.expected:
"example.net. 7200 IN SOA ns1.example.net. hostmaster.example.net. 2023110101 10800 3600 604800 10800
example.net. 7200 IN NS ns1.example.net.
example.net. 7200 IN MX 10 mail.example.net.
example.net. 7200 IN TXT "v=spf1 include:_spf.example.net ~all"
"
cases.description: Add a full set of typical records (SOA, NS, MX, TXT) to verify that toString() correctly concatenates different RR types while preserving the order and proper spacing.

Force toMasterFile() to throw an IOException (e.g., by mocking a Zone subclass where toMasterFile() throws). toString() should not catch the exception; the same IOException must be propagated to the caller.
Create a Zone, add a few records (e.g., SOA, NS, A). Call toString() twice and verify that both returned strings are exactly equal, proving that toString() does not mutate internal state.

group: Zone after removal of a record

cases.expected: "example.org. 3600 IN NS ns1.example.org.\nexample.org. 3600 IN NS ns2.example.org.\n"
cases.description: Add two NS records and one A record, then remove the A record via removeRecord(). The master‑file representation returned by toString() must contain only the two NS lines, confirming that removal is reflected.

group: Multiple records of the same name and type (A)

cases.description: Add two A records for the same host name. toString() must emit both lines in the order they were added, demonstrating that the zone stores multiple RRs of the same type.

group: Order preservation when mixing addRRset and addRecord

cases.description: Create an RRset containing an MX record and add it with addRRset(). Then add an A record with addRecord(). toString() must list the MX line first followed by the A line, confirming that insertion order across the two APIs is respected.
Add an A record with a TTL of 0. The master‑file line produced by toString() must contain the literal "0" as the TTL, proving that zero TTLs are serialized correctly.

Add 50 distinct A records (e.g., host0.example.com … host49.example.com). toString() should contain exactly 50 newline‑terminated lines. The test asserts the count of '\n' characters equals 50, ensuring scalability.
After populating a Zone with a variety of records, invoke both zone.toString() and zone.toMasterFile(). The two returned strings must be equal, confirming that toString() is a pure delegate.
Create a subclass of Zone that overrides toMasterFile() to throw a new IllegalStateException. Calling toString() must propagate this unchecked exception unchanged.

Populate a Zone with several records, then start a background thread that adds/removes records while the main thread invokes zone.toString(). The internal iteration performed by toMasterFile() should detect the concurrent modification and throw ConcurrentModificationException, which must be propagated by toString().

Create a subclass of Zone that sets its internal data structures (e.g., the map that stores RRsets) to null before calling toString(). When toMasterFile() attempts to iterate over the null collection, a NullPointerException should be thrown and propagated.
